frozen_candidate_root_contribution: In its veracity family (Forms I, II, the abstract sidq, the intensive siddiq, and the elative asdaq: ~128/155), s-d-q = the conformity of a word - a claim, report, promise, prediction, or the revealed message - to reality; derivationally, being the person or proposition that so conforms (opposite of kadhib), and, in Form II, the factitive act of affirming/attesting/making such a word conform to reality. This account is representative of the dominant family only; it does NOT reach the almsgiving/gift field or the frozen 'friend' lexeme.

This account is representative of the dominant family only; it does NOT reach the almsgiving/gift field or the frozen 'friend' lexeme.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The core of this root is truth as correspondence: a statement, promise or vision that matches the facts, or a person whose word matches reality - the standing opposite of lying. The Quran extends this in a regular way: to keep or make-good a promise (bringing reality into line with one's word), and in the 'saddaqa' form to affirm or confirm something as true (scripture 'confirming' earlier scripture). But the same consonants also carry two senses the Quran never links back to truth: giving - alms, charity, remitting a debt or blood-money, and the bridal gift - and simply 'friend'. Because the text itself lists 'the truthful' and 'the almsgivers' side by side as different virtues (33:35), we report a strong core for the truth family and treat giving and friend as separate, unbridged classes rather than forcing them into one meaning.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Sdq is NOT mere assertion (that is q-w-l); it adds conformity-to-fact, hence its fixed antonymy with kadhib (12:26; 27:27). It is NOT full iman/trust-commitment: saddaqa bi- (credence) is conjoined with, and narrower than, amana (2:41; 57:19). It is NOT generic righteousness: siddiqin are ranked beside, not within, salihin/nabiyyin (4:69; 19:41). It is NOT morally loaded: 34:20 lets Iblis's conjecture 'come true'. Crucially, veracity does NOT entail giving and giving does NOT entail truth-value (33:35), and the construct 'X of sidq' (10:2; 19:50) means 'genuine/well-founded X', not literal speech, yet still 'real, not false'.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 4:4 'saduqatihinna nihlatan' (the obligatory bridal gift) - a root-nominal denoting a marriage payment with no assertoric, fulfillment, or faith content, unassimilable to veracity by any Quran-internal step. It is backed by the whole almsgiving field, of which 9:60 'innama al-sadaqatu lil-fuqara'' is representative (a fiscal distribution category), and by 26:101 'wa-la sadiqin hamim' (friend). These defeat any claim that the root is semantically unified around truth. The sharpest strain INSIDE the family is 37:105 'saddaqta al-ru'ya' (Form II used for 'fulfilled the vision'), which collapses the II-declarative vs I-fulfil boundary but remains within the correspondence nucleus.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: A single super-gloss 'genuineness / bringing-into-accord-with-the-real': true speech = genuine speech; keeping a promise = making one's word real; sadaqah = the gift that realizes/authenticates faith; saduqat = the gift that makes a marriage binding; sadiq = a genuine/loyal companion. It is rejected as the operative account because (a) no verse glosses charity, dowry, or friendship in truth/genuineness terms - the verses use nihlah (4:4), hamim (26:101), zakat/qard (58:13; 57:18) with no truth-semantics; (b) 33:35 actively separates the truthful from the almsgivers; and (c) it is exactly the 'vague abstraction that fits everything' the methodology forbids and violates the narrowness rule. It is recorded only as the strongest competitor.

It is rejected as the operative account because (a) no verse glosses charity, dowry, or friendship in truth/genuineness terms - the verses use nihlah (4:4), hamim (26:101), zakat/qard (58:13; 57:18) with no truth-semantics; (b) 33:35 actively separates the truthful from the almsgivers; and (c) it is exactly the 'vague abstraction that fits everything' the methodology forbids and violates the narrowness rule. internal_discovery.rationale: Three independent lenses converged: a broad, distinctive, adversarially-clean veracity nucleus covers ~128/155 (Form I speak-truly/be-true-to/fulfil; participle sadiq = true speaker or true proposition, incl. 51:5 of the promised thing; abstract sidq and the 'X of sidq' idiom; intensive siddiq; elative asdaq = truer-in-speech, 4:87; and Form II as the transparent factitive 'affirm/confirm/realize true'). Internal bridges are demonstrable: sadaqa...al-wa'd spans speech and promise-fulfilment; sadiqa al-wa'd (19:54) ties participle to fulfilment; 39:33 pairs sidq (nucleus) with saddaqa bi- (Form II) in one verse; Form II keeps the kadhib antonym (75:31). But STRONG/UNIVERSAL is barred: the giving field (~25 occ) is a coherent, sizeable, internally-varied (donation vs remission vs obligatory dowry) lexicalized class whose contrast set is withholding/riba, never lying; and 'friend' (2 occ) is a frozen lexeme. Neither is bridged to veracity without importing etymology. Under the contract a coherent resistant lexicalized sub-class caps the ROOT-level result at MODERATE / REPRESENTATIVE, reported as a dominant veracity family plus at least two unbridged lexicalized classes - not a forced unity and not a failure.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Conformity of a word/claim/report/promise/vision/revealed message to reality, and the person or proposition that so conforms (opposite of kadhib): Form I verb (speak-truly, be-true-to, fulfil a promise/vision, e.g. 48:27, 21:9, 33:23), active participle sadiq/sadiqin (true speaker or true proposition, 51:5; incl. the challenge-formula in kuntum sadiqin), abstract sidq (truthfulness; 'the truth', 39:32; and the idiom 'X of sidq' = genuine/well-founded X, 10:2, 19:50, 54:55), intensive siddiq (eminently veracious rank, 19:41, 4:69), and elative asdaq (truer in speech, 4:87).
clusters.classification_rationale: Repeated explicit antonymy with kadhib (12:26; 27:27; 9:43; 40:28) fixes the sense as truth-as-correspondence; cross-form collocations (sadaqa+al-wa'd; sadiqa al-wa'd 19:54) show speech and promise-fulfilment are one field; the 'X of sidq' idiom still reduces to 'real, not false'. Adversarially clean within this family.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 12:26 fa-sadaqat vs al-kadhibin; 4:87 asdaqu min Allahi hadithan locks the core to truth-of-utterance; 5:119 yanfa'u al-sadiqina siduquhum; 19:54 sadiqa al-wa'd bridges participle to fulfilment; 51:5 predicates sadiq of the promised thing itself.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Factitive/declarative branch of the nucleus: to hold/affirm/attest something as true, give credence to (saddaqa bi- 39:33, 92:6, 70:26; transitive saddaqa al-mursalin 37:37); muSaddiq = scripture confirming prior scripture as true (2:41, 3:3, 61:6); taSdiq = a confirmation (10:37, 12:111); with a causative edge 'make/prove true by outcome' (34:20 Iblis's conjecture; 37:105 fulfilling the vision).
clusters.classification_rationale: Morphologically the transparent factitive of the nucleus; Quran-internally bridged by 39:33, which pairs ja'a bi-al-sidq (nucleus) with wa-saddaqa bihi (Form II) in one verse, and by the retained kadhib antonym (75:31 fa-la saddaqa ... wa-lakin kadhdhaba). Distinct from iman (2:41 conjoins amana with muSaddiqan) and from abrogation (muSaddiq held apart from muhaymin, 5:48).
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 39:33:4:2 wa-saddaqa bihi beside 39:33:3:3 bi-al-sidq is the decisive intra-verse bridge; 2:41 muSaddiqan li-ma ma'akum; 34:20 and 37:105 mark the causative boundary where II converges with the Form I 'fulfil' pole (48:27).

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: A self-contained benefaction/transfer field with no truth-value semantics: noun sadaqah/sadaqat = alms as a fiscal distribution category (9:60; 9:103), Form V taSaddaqa = give, or remit a due (alms 2:280; retaliation 5:45; blood-money 4:92; begging for grain 12:88), N(V) mutaSaddiq = almsgivers (33:35; 57:18 paired with lending to God), plus the sub-sense saduqat = obligatory bridal gift (4:4).
clusters.classification_rationale: Its contrast set is generosity vs withholding/riba (2:276), never truth vs lie. The Quran never uses taSaddaqa/sadaqah for 'affirm true', and 33:35 lists the almsgivers separately from the truthful. The bridge to veracity is etymological only, so under QURAN-INTERNAL-ONLY it is a distinct lexicalized class. Note internal variation: donation vs remission-of-a-due vs obligatory dowry.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 9:60 innama al-sadaqatu lil-fuqara'; 2:276 yamhaqu al-riba wa-yurbi al-sadaqat pins the antonym as withholding, not lying; 4:4 saduqatihinna nihlatan; 57:18 al-mussaddiqin ... wa-aqradu Allaha qardan hasanan (giving = lending).

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Frozen relational noun sadiq = 'friend/intimate', with no veracity content recoverable from context.
clusters.classification_rationale: 24:61 lists sadiq among kin whose houses one may eat in; 26:101 wa-la sadiqin hamim pairs it with 'intimate'. No verse glosses it toward truthfulness; per 'same root != one meaning', it is a lexicalized homonymous class.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 26:101:2:1 wa-la sadiqin hamim; 24:61:49:1 aw sadiqikum - both purely relational.

reconciliation.rationale: 48:27 (Form I) sadaqa Allahu rasulahu al-ru'ya applies the same 'make-good the vision' sense, so 37:105 is the factitive of the very fulfil-pole already inside the nucleus, not a new sense.
Same verse pairs ja'a bi-al-sidq (nucleus) with wa-saddaqa bihi (Form II), demonstrating the Quran-internal bridge; Form II is the factitive branch, not a distinct class.
That reading is etymological/external; Quran-internally 9:60 frames sadaqah fiscally and 33:35 separates almsgivers from the truthful, so it must be recorded as an unbridged lexicalized class.

adversarial_verification.notes: A formal PASSED adversarial refutation is not claimed because the account is deliberately scoped to the veracity family and does NOT cover the giving (25) and friend (2) classes, which resist. The core survived adversarial probing (34:20 moral-neutrality boundary; 37:105 II/I convergence; 39:33 bridge), but because material occurrences resist, status is NOT_RUN with the resisting occurrences recorded rather than PASSED.

occurrence_dispositions.note: Its contrast set is generosity vs withholding/riba (2:276), never truth vs lie. The Quran never uses taSaddaqa/sadaqah for 'affirm true', and 33:35 lists the almsgivers separately from the truthful. The bridge to veracity is etymological only, so under QURAN-INTERNAL-ONLY it is a distinct lexicalized class. Note internal variation: donation vs remission-of-a-due vs obligatory dowry.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: A self-contained benefaction/transfer field with no truth-value semantics: noun sadaqah/sadaqat = alms as a fiscal distribution category (9:60; 9:103), Form V taSaddaqa = give, or remit a due (alms 2:280; retaliation 5:45; blood-money 4:92; begging for grain 12:88), N(V) mutaSaddiq = almsgivers (33:35; 57:18 paired with lending to God), plus the sub-sense saduqat = obligatory bridal gift (4:4).
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 9:60 innama al-sadaqatu lil-fuqara'; 2:276 yamhaqu al-riba wa-yurbi al-sadaqat pins the antonym as withholding, not lying; 4:4 saduqatihinna nihlatan; 57:18 al-mussaddiqin ... wa-aqradu Allaha qardan hasanan (giving = lending).

occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: A self-contained benefaction/transfer field with no truth-value semantics: noun sadaqah/sadaqat = alms as a fiscal distribution category (9:60; 9:103), Form V taSaddaqa = give, or remit a due (alms 2:280; retaliation 5:45; blood-money 4:92; begging for grain 12:88), N(V) mutaSaddiq = almsgivers (33:35; 57:18 paired with lending to God), plus the sub-sense saduqat = obligatory bridal gift (4:4).

The bridge to veracity is etymological only, so under QURAN-INTERNAL-ONLY it is a distinct lexicalized class. Note internal variation: donation vs remission-of-a-due vs obligatory dowry.

The Quran never uses taSaddaqa/sadaqah for 'affirm true', and 33:35 lists the almsgivers separately from the truthful. The bridge to veracity is etymological only, so under QURAN-INTERNAL-ONLY it is a distinct lexicalized class. Note internal variation: donation vs remission-of-a-due vs obligatory dowry.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: A self-contained benefaction/transfer field with no truth-value semantics: noun sadaqah/sadaqat = alms as a fiscal distribution category (9:60; 9:103), Form V taSaddaqa = give, or remit a due (alms 2:280; retaliation 5:45; blood-money 4:92; begging for grain 12:88), N(V) mutaSaddiq = almsgivers (33:35; 57:18 paired with lending to God), plus the sub-sense saduqat = obligatory bridal gift (4:4).

occurrence_dispositions.verse_text: وَصَدَّقَ بِٱلْحُسْنَىٰ

occurrence_dispositions.note: Its contrast set is generosity vs withholding/riba (2:276), never truth vs lie. The Quran never uses taSaddaqa/sadaqah for 'affirm true', and 33:35 lists the almsgivers separately from the truthful. independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) converged on the same partition, the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE grade, and the same resistant classes.
candidate_root_contribution: In its veracity family (Forms I, II, the abstract sidq, the intensive siddiq, and the elative asdaq: ~128/155), s-d-q = the conformity of a word - a claim, report, promise, prediction, or the revealed message - to reality; derivationally, being the person or proposition that so conforms (opposite of kadhib), and, in Form II, the factitive act of affirming/attesting/making such a word conform to reality. This account is representative of the dominant family only; it does NOT reach the almsgiving/gift field or the frozen 'friend' lexeme.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: Direct usage: Form I with kadhib antonym (12:26, 27:27, 9:43); sadaqa+al-wa'd fulfilment (21:9, 48:27, 33:23); challenge-formula in kuntum sadiqin; sidq abstract (5:119, 39:32); giving usage (9:60, 9:103, 2:280, 5:45); friend (24:61, 26:101).
layer_attribution.derivation: Form II is the transparent factitive of the nucleus (affirm/realize-true), bridged intra-verse at 39:33; Form V and the sadaqah noun are the reflexive/nominal derivations that carry the SEPARATE giving sense - derivation is noted but morphology is not treated as semantic identity.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: Two lexicalized classes are held apart from the root claim: the giving/gift field (alms, remission, dowry) and the frozen relational noun sadiq (friend). Their link to truth is external/etymological only.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: Narrative/enumerative context (33:35 listing virtues; 57:18->57:19 adjacency of almsgivers and the veracious) is used to SEPARATE senses, and is explicitly NOT elevated into the root claim; adjacency is not derivation.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: Preliminary tensions (37:105, 39:33 Form II status; the 'genuineness' super-gloss for alms) were resolved by intra-verse bridges for the nucleus and by 33:35's positive separation for the giving class.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: The giving field (~25 occ) and friend lexeme (2 occ) remain Quran-internally unbridged to veracity and are carried as persistent resistance capping the root-level grade at MODERATE / REPRESENTATIVE.

hard_case_representation.rationale: The giving/almsgiving/gift field (25 occ) and the friend lexeme (2 occ) persist as Quran-internally unbridged classes and are reported as RESISTANT_SEAM hard cases rather than assimilated. Two further within-family occurrences (37:105 causative-fulfil; 34:20 morally-neutral correspondence) are retained as STRUCTURAL_ATYPICALITY / ADVERSARIAL_BOUNDARY probes that were tested and confirmed to lie inside the nucleus.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A Quran-internal verse that glosses, derives, or predicates the giving field (sadaqah/taSaddaqa/saduqat) or the friend lexeme (sadiq) in terms of truth-conformity - e.g. calling an almsgiver 'truthful' BECAUSE they give, or a friend 'true' in a verifiable-claim sense - which would collapse the resistant classes into the veracity nucleus and push the scope toward UNIVERSAL.
rejection_condition.search_location: The giving cluster (qac_verb_form V plus sadaqah/saduqat nouns: 9:60, 9:103, 2:263-2:276, 12:88, 2:280, 5:45, 4:92, 57:18, 63:10, 9:75, 33:35:14-15, 4:4) and the friend cluster (24:61, 26:101), read against the veracity anchors (33:35 juxtaposition, 39:33 bridge).
rejection_condition.verification_method: Check each candidate for an explicit intra-verse semantic link (shared predicate, gloss, or kadhib-antonymy) between a giving/friend form and truth-conformity, not mere co-occurrence, adjacency (57:18->57:19), or shared consonantal root.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Exclude etymological/lexicographic priors and classical unification ('charity proves sincerity'); exclude morphological identity as evidence of semantic identity; exclude narrative adjacency; require a Quran-internal predication, since 33:35 positively separates the two virtues.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If no such bridge is found, the giving and friend classes remain RESISTANT and the root-level result stays MODERATE / REPRESENTATIVE (dominant veracity family + unbridged lexicalized classes); if a genuine bridge IS found, reopen toward a broader scope.

reopen_conditions: If a Quran-internal verse is found predicating sadaqah/taSaddaqa or saduqat (4:4) in truth-conformity terms (e.g. an almsgiver called sadiq BECAUSE of giving), re-test whether the giving field bridges into the veracity nucleus and the scope should widen.
If sadiq (24:61; 26:101) is shown by any verse to carry a verifiable-claim/loyalty-as-truth sense rather than a frozen relational noun, reopen the friend class as bridged.

If the Form II causative pole (34:20 saddaqa 'alayhim ... zannahu; 37:105 saddaqta al-ru'ya) is judged to split off as a distinct 'make-come-true' class rather than the factitive of the fulfil-pole, re-cluster Form II.
If the 'X of sidq' construct idiom (10:2 qadama sidq; 19:50 lisana sidq; 54:55 maq'adi sidq) is shown to be a lexicalized honorific class not reducible to 'real, not false', re-scope the sidq noun.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: A formal PASSED adversarial refutation is not claimed because the account is deliberately scoped to the veracity family and does NOT cover the giving (25) and friend (2) classes, which resist. The core survived adversarial probing (34:20 moral-neutrality boundary; 37:105 II/I convergence; 39:33 bridge), but because material occurrences resist, status is NOT_RUN with the resisting occurrences recorded rather than PASSED.
